title: Route-level A/B testing — Experiment Results Dashboard Mockups (Grafana) v0.4
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Route-level A/B testing: Experiment Results Dashboards (Grafana)
Mockups + panel inventory + query notes
Owner: Observability (Allison, Aisha)

Speaker notes:
- These are mockups for the initial beta. Goal is: ship something usable + safe; we can iterate fast once the schema + ingestion are stable.
- This deck is written for ENG-2845 (dashboards + alerts), but references results UI requirements in Console (DES-143) to keep naming consistent.


Slide 2 — What questions should the dashboard answer?
1) Is the experiment healthy?
- Is error rate up? Timeouts? 429s? elevated cancellations?
- Is latency regressing (p95/p99, TTFT)?

2) What is the economic impact?
- $/1k tokens (effective), GPU cost attribution per request, token usage shifts
- Is variant B cheaper but slower? or vice versa

3) Is traffic split behaving?
- Exposure volume by variant vs configured split
- Exposure sampling status and dropped events

4) Drill-down for triage
- Region / route / customer tier / model / variant
- "what changed?" correlations (deploys, policy edits, capacity constrains)

Speaker notes:
- Avoid building a mini-Console in Grafana; focus on fast triage and SRE guardrails. Console will own the deeper experiment reporting.


Slide 3 — Assumptions & data sources (v1)
Metrics / events we assume exist (schema v1):
- exposure events emitted from gateway: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, project_id (or project hash), region, status
- request latency metrics: e2e_ms, ttft_ms, stream_duration_ms (if available)
- counts: requests, successes, 4xx, 5xx, timeouts, cancellations
- cost attribution: token_in, token_out, tokens_total, gpu_ms (or gpu_cost_usd), cost_usd

Queryable dimensions we will support (cardinality reviewed):
- experiment_id (required)
- variant_id (required)
- region (allowed list)
- route_id (stable, not raw path)
- model_id (stable slug)

Explicitly NOT supported as dashboard dimensions (v1):
- raw user_id, raw api_key_id, raw prompt template IDs (too high cardinality)
- request_id (drill-down via logs instead)

Speaker notes:
- This aligns with the cardinality review doc + PR 18519 allowlist approach.
- Console team asked about project_id filtering; recommendation is: only in Console or use hashed_project_id in Grafana if absolutely needed.


Slide 4 — Dashboard #1: Experiment Overview (default landing)
Layout (top to bottom):
A) Header row / controls
- Experiment: dropdown (experiment_id)
- Time range picker
- Filters: variant_id (multi), region (multi), model_id (multi), route_id (single)
- Links: "Open in Console" (deep link w/ experiment_id), "Runbook" (disable/rollback)

B) KPI row (single-stat)
- Requests/min (overall)
- Exposure count/min (by variant)
- Error rate (overall + by variant)
- p95 latency (e2e_ms) (overall + by variant)
- p95 TTFT (ttft_ms)
- Cost per request (avg, by variant)

C) Trends row (time series)
- Requests & exposures by variant (two axes, or stacked area)
- p50/p95 e2e latency by variant
- p50/p95 TTFT by variant
- Error rate by variant (stacked: 4xx vs 5xx vs timeout)
- Cost per request by variant

Speaker notes:
- Strong preference: keep the landing lightweight and readable on-call.
- The biggest "trust" issue is mismatch between configured split and actual exposures; we should make that obvious.


Slide 5 — Panel mock: Traffic split + exposure sanity
Panel: "Exposure volume by variant (stacked)"
- Graph: stacked area per variant_id
- Overlay line: total requests/min (from request metrics)

Panel: "Observed split vs configured split"
- Table:
  - variant_id
  - observed_exposure_pct (last 15m, 1h, 24h)
  - configured_pct (from control plane config scrape; see note)
  - delta (observed - configured)
  - sample_rate (if exposures are sampled)

Notes / gotchas:
- If exposure events are sampled, the observed_exposure_pct is unbiased if sampling is uniform across variants.
- If we sample on request outcome (e.g. only successes), that will bias; we should not do that.
- Configured_pct source: either (a) synthetic metric emitted by control plane on publish OR (b) scrape config from assignment service and export as metrics. Option (a) is cleaner.

Speaker notes:
- This is the panel that catches the "variant B traffic is higher than configured" bug (see earlier staging thread).


Slide 6 — Panel mock: Latency comparison (variant A vs B)
Panel group: "Latency distribution"
1) Time series: p50/p95/p99 e2e_ms by variant
2) Time series: p50/p95/p99 ttft_ms by variant
3) Histogram: e2e_ms distribution (overlay A/B)

Annotations:
- Mark experiment start/stop times
- Mark rollout/policy changes if we can ingest audit events as annotations (future)

Suggested default time windows:
- Last 1h (high resolution)
- Last 24h (trend)

Speaker notes:
- Console will do deeper statistical comparisons, but Grafana should show if p95 is trending up right now.
- TTFT should be first-class because it’s what users complain about for streaming.


Slide 7 — Panel mock: Errors & reliability
Panel group: "Errors / timeouts / throttling"
- Stacked time series: rate of status_class (2xx, 4xx, 5xx) by variant
- Separate time series: 429 rate by variant (call out capacity issues)
- Separate time series: timeout rate (gateway timeout / upstream timeout if split exists)
- Heatmap: errors by region (rows=region, columns=variant, value=error_rate)

Text callouts (top right):
- "Guardrail status: PASS/WARN/FAIL" computed from thresholds (see SLO policy)

Speaker notes:
- Incident we saw: experiment routed more traffic to constrained capacity in one region -> 429s. Make 429 panel prominent.


Slide 8 — Panel mock: Cost & usage
Panel group: "Cost attribution"
- Time series: avg cost_usd/request by variant
- Time series: avg tokens_total/request by variant
- Time series: avg gpu_ms/request by variant (if present)
- Scatter plot: requests (x=tokens_total, y=e2e_ms, color=variant) sampled (if Grafana supports)

Table: "Economics summary (selected window)"
- variant_id
- requests
- avg_tokens_in / avg_tokens_out
- avg_cost_usd/request
- cost_per_1k_tokens (effective)
- p95_e2e_ms
- error_rate

Speaker notes:
- Nadia requested we present $/1k tokens because it normalizes across prompt length differences.
- If we can’t get gpu_ms reliably across Hosted/Dedicated, keep it behind a conditional panel.


Slide 9 — Drill-down dashboard #2: Experiment Debug / Triage
Purpose: get from "alert fired" to "what is broken" quickly.

Sections:
A) Breakdown by region
- small multiples: p95 latency + error rate per region (lines A/B)
- table: top regions by delta(p95) and delta(error)

B) Breakdown by route_id (if experiment covers multiple routes; probably rare)
- table: route_id, requests, p95, error_rate, delta

C) Breakdown by model_id / config
- table: model_id, quant_profile (if available), max_tokens buckets (if available), p95, cost

D) Log pivots (links)
- Link out to logs explorer with experiment_id + variant_id filters

Speaker notes:
- We should be careful about exploding queries. Keep drill-down to top N (e.g., top 10 regions/routes).


Slide 10 — Alerting mockups (guardrails)
Alert class 1: Hard stop / page SRE
- Condition: error_rate_variant > threshold for >= 5m OR 429_rate_variant spike
- Action: page on-call + notify #eng-sre + create incident if sustained

Alert class 2: Soft guardrail (notify owning team + Console banner)
- Condition: p95_e2e_ms_variant delta vs control > X% for >= 10m
- Action: Slack to #eng-platform + create ticket; optional automation hook to rollback if configured

Alert class 3: Data quality
- Condition: exposures missing (exposure_rate << request_rate) OR exposure schema version mismatch
- Action: notify observability + platform

Threshold placeholders (needs Sean signoff):
- p95 regression: +15% warn, +25% fail (window 10m)
- error rate: +0.5% absolute warn, +1.0% absolute fail (window 5m)
- 429: any sustained > baseline + 0.2% absolute (window 5m)

Speaker notes:
- Guardrails should be per-experiment to avoid paging on every experiment launch across the fleet.
- When possible, compare variant vs control, not vs global baseline.


Slide 11 — UI copy / naming consistency (Grafana vs Console)
Proposed naming:
- "Control" = variant with baseline config (often A)
- "Treatment" = variant under test (often B)
- But in UI always show explicit variant_id and allow custom label.

Panel labels:
- Use "TTFT" not "time to first token" everywhere
- Use "e2e latency" for overall request duration

Notes:
- Support thread mentioned confusion around "control" semantics. In Grafana, prefer: "Variant A (control)" if label exists; otherwise just A/B.


Slide 12 — Open questions / TODOs
1) Configured split source
- Do we emit configured split as a metric on experiment start/update? (preferred)
- Alternative: scrape assignment service (adds dependency)

2) Exposure sampling
- Confirm sampling strategy is uniform and tagged with sample_rate
- Need panel for "sample_rate" so people don’t misread absolute counts

3) Metric naming finalization
- Need final names for: e2e_ms, ttft_ms, cost_usd, gpu_ms, timeout_count
- Align with ab-testing-metrics-schema-v1

4) Cross-environment support
- Hosted + Dedicated: OK
- Private: likely later; but dashboard should not assume hosted-only dimensions

5) Annotations
- Can we ingest audit events (create/update/start/stop/rollback) as Grafana annotations keyed by experiment_id?

Owners (tentative):
- Allison: dashboard layouts + alert definitions
- Aisha: thresholds + on-call routing + runbook links
- Logan/Nadia: confirm metric availability + cost naming
- Vikram/Amara: confirm gateway emits required tags


Slide 13 — Appendix: Proposed panel inventory (for ENG-2845)
Experiment Overview dashboard (must-have):
- Requests/min by variant
- Exposures/min by variant
- Observed split vs configured split (table)
- p50/p95/p99 e2e latency by variant
- p50/p95/p99 TTFT by variant
- Error rate by variant (4xx/5xx/timeout)
- 429 rate by variant
- Avg cost/request by variant
- Avg tokens_total/request by variant

Experiment Debug dashboard (nice-to-have for beta, likely required for GA):
- Region breakdown (p95, error_rate, 429)
- Model breakdown (p95, cost)
- Data quality panels (exposure missing, schema mismatch)

Alert rules (beta minimum):
- p95 regression alert (variant vs control)
- error rate alert (variant vs control)
- 429 rate spike alert
- exposure missing / ingestion broken alert


Slide 14 — Appendix: Rough query patterns (placeholder)
NOTE: pseudo-queries; actual depends on TSDB naming (Prometheus vs Mimir, etc.)

Latency (p95) by variant:
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_bucket{experiment_id="$exp"}[5m])) by (le, variant_id))

Error rate by variant:
- sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{experiment_id="$exp", status_class!="2xx"}[5m])) by (variant_id)
  /
  sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{experiment_id="$exp"}[5m])) by (variant_id)

Cost per request by variant:
- sum(rate(redwood_cost_usd_total{experiment_id="$exp"}[5m])) by (variant_id)
  /
  sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{experiment_id="$exp"}[5m])) by (variant_id)

Observed split:
- sum(rate(redwood_exposures_total{experiment_id="$exp"}[5m])) by (variant_id)
  /
  sum(rate(redwood_exposures_total{experiment_id="$exp"}[5m]))

Speaker notes:
- The point is: keep it simple, avoid massive group-bys, use experiment_id as the anchor.


Slide 15 — Appendix: Screenshot placeholders

- Wireframe: Debug dashboard (desktop)

Notes:
